item.title: Texas Jury Finds No Legal or Informal Adoption in $1 Million Inheritance Dispute
item.description: In a complex Texas inheritance case, a stepson referred to as 'my child' in a will navigated a treacherous dispute following his father's passing. Despite his claims of informal adoption, the family remained unconvinced. Ultimately, the jury affirmed that no formal or informal adoption occurred. This outcome highlights the necessity of clear legal documentation in estate planning to avoid misunderstandings, particularly within blended families concerning rights to inheritance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Steven Spielberg pulls $29.9 M LA ranch off the market
item.description: Filmmaker Steven Spielberg listed his Los Angeles ranch for $29.9 million but has now taken it off the market. He and his wife purchased the property in 1999 for $5.75 million, intending to create equestrian facilities. After facing opposition from local residents, their renovation plans were significantly reduced over the years. The ranch, known as Dogwood, features a main house with numerous upscale amenities and a 20,000-square-foot riding arena.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: In 1600, William Gilbert called Earth a giant magnet; his book sold for Rs 58.5 lakh in 2026
item.description: William Gilbert's pivotal publication, De Magnete, emerged in 1600, marking a significant shift in the exploration of magnetism and electricity. It introduced key terms and experimental approaches that influenced future electrical studies. The concept of Earth as a colossal magnet was groundbreaking. Recently, a first edition fetched $61,440 at a Christie’s auction, highlighting its enduring significance and the continued fascination it holds in scientific discourse.

item.title: In 2022, conservators X-raying a Van Gogh painting in Edinburgh found a hidden self-portrait of the artist on the back of the canvas, concealed for more than a century under layers of glue and cardboard
item.description: A self-portrait of Vincent van Gogh was discovered concealed behind another painting after many years. The hidden portrait was found during routine examinations ahead of an exhibition. This discovery highlights Van Gogh's habit of reusing canvases due to financial difficulties throughout his life. Conservators are now working to reveal the portrait without damaging the original painting. Visitors to the exhibition were able to view the hidden portrait's X-ray image.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: A community in South Australia’s first dark-sky reserve is opposing a proposed hyperscale data centre; residents fear the development could change the rural landscape and threaten the darkness that draws visitors
item.description: Residents of Tungkillo, South Australia, are concerned about a proposed data centre that could disrupt their dark-sky reserve. The development may introduce light and noise pollution that affects the rural landscape. Community members believe preserving their unique nighttime environment is crucial for stargazing and natural experiences. The project's economic benefits are being weighed against potential environmental impacts. Ongoing discussions will determine the future of digital infrastructure in the region.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: The asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs 66 million years ago may have also set the stage for ants to conquer the planet, with scientists finding a surprising boost from so-called jumping genes hidden in ant DNA
item.description: Since the dinosaurs vanished, ants have flourished, with more than 15,000 species recognized globally. New research, spearheaded by Dr. Lukas Schrader, highlights the role of jumping genes in their evolution and resilience. Significant surges of these genes occurred during the early Paleogene period, enhancing ants' olfactory receptors and social communication skills, thus providing a genetic edge for survival in diverse environments.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Texas homeowners win control of their park, roads and ponds after a decade-long legal battle
item.description: In a significant turn of events, residents of La Bota Ranch in Laredo officially gained control over common property areas after a protracted legal battle. This shift follows a jury's March 2022 decision that found developers had breached fiduciary duties, prompting residents to reevaluate governance due to rising association fees. The final handover on August 20, 2026, empowers homeowners over shared facilities, symbolizing a hard-won victory for community representation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A 3,106-carat diamond pulled from a South African mine became the 530-carat gem in Britain's royal sceptre
item.description: Frederick Wells discovered the enormous Cullinan diamond in South Africa in 1905 while working at the Premier Mine. Its exceptional size caught public attention, leading to its purchase by the Transvaal government for King Edward VII. The diamond was carefully cut into several gemstones over eight months, resulting in noteworthy pieces for the British royal collection. Following Edward VII's death, the largest stone was incorporated into the Sovereign's Sceptre.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An Indy charity started in 2016 with $9k raised in 45 mins; 10 yrs on, it reached 175k bouquets
item.description: Random Acts of Flowers Indianapolis marked ten years of service, delivering its 175,000th flower arrangement to Eskenazi Health. This charity reuses donated flowers to create arrangements for hospital patients in need. Volunteers collect flowers from various local sources to prevent waste and support emotional well-being. The organization was founded after a successful fundraising effort in 2016. It aims to continue its work through community partnerships and ongoing donations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Newly identified bird like dinosaur from Cretaceous period may be first dinosaur eating fruit
item.description: Scientists have recently uncovered a small dinosaur named Infernogallus jamesi, believed to have predominantly dined on fruit. By examining its skull and jaw muscles, researchers gained insights into its dietary habits. Existing during the Cretaceous period, as flowering plants flourished, this dinosaur displays anatomical traits akin to modern fruit-feeding parrots, deepening our comprehension of the varied lifestyles in the era of dinosaurs.
item.dc:creator: TOI Lifestyle Desk

item.title: Royal regret! British king 'recognises' slavery horrors amid his Caribbean tour
item.description: Despite the pressure, Buckingham Palace has said Charles will not issue an apology during the tour, arguing that such matters are “matters for governments to address”. The palace added that he would “not shy away from the darkest days of our past.” As monarch, Charles represents Britain abroad on the advice of the government.
item.dc:creator: Rajeev Singh

item.title: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show clear signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists have found an important clue hidden in a rare group of resilient brains
item.description: Recent research from the Netherlands Institute for Neuroscience has revealed intriguing findings about Alzheimer's disease. Scientists examined brain tissues from different groups, including those with and without dementia symptoms. They discovered that immature neurons acted differently in cognitively healthy individuals despite Alzheimer's brain changes. This suggests that these neurons may play a role in supporting brain function rather than simply replacing damaged cells.

item.title: Mississippi father gives wife home promised to three children; daughter loses court battle
item.description: A Mississippi father left his family home and 0.86 acres of land equally to his three children in a 2008 will but transferred the property to his wife in 2021. After his death, his daughter challenged the transfer, claiming he had been improperly influenced due to his declining health. On Tuesday, an appeals court rejected her challenge, finding insufficient evidence of undue influence.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Minecraft creator lists Beverly Hills estate for $70M
item.description: Markus 'Notch' Persson has placed his Beverly Hills mansion on the market for $70 million. He purchased the estate in 2014 after outbidding Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who also showed interest. The mansion features eight bedrooms, a nightclub, and a professional recording studio for entertainment. The billionaire decided to sell as he spends less time in Los Angeles these days.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Wildlife traffickers may have killed her family to capture her; rescued baby gorilla Bili begins a second life in Congo
item.description: Bili, the young gorilla saved from wildlife trafficking in Nigeria, has embarked on a fresh journey in the Republic of the Congo. After three years of dedicated care and rehabilitation, she is now set for a quarantine period at the Tchimpounga Nature Reserve. Here, Bili will undergo health assessments and prepare for her introduction to fellow gorillas, with hopes of eventually reintegrating her into the wild.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
